note: Development material: rules and facts were written and adjusted while looking at these trees. Not an accuracy estimate.

rules.title: one command persists two or more aggregate-root instances in one synchronous flow
rules.rule: One command changes and saves one aggregate instance; any other aggregate is updated later, by a handler of a domain event the first one records (Vernon, Effective Aggregate Design).
rules.fix: Save only the aggregate this command changes; have it record a domain event (stored with it, as the outbox does) and update the other aggregate(s) in a handler of that event.
rules.applies: aggregate roots declared in the spec's DDD block (or inferred: identity-bearing domain types taken by a repository port)

rules.title: a business decision about an aggregate is taken outside the aggregate
rules.rule: An invariant of an aggregate is checked inside the aggregate (its method or a value object), so no caller can bypass or duplicate it (Vernon: model true invariants in consistency boundaries).
rules.fix: Move the check into the aggregate method that changes the state (or into a value object it takes) and let the service call that method; keep one copy of the rule.
rules.applies: aggregate roots declared (or inferred); application and adapter code only

rules.title: a published contract is, or wraps, a domain entity (or the domain builds the contract's shape)
rules.rule: The published language of a context is its own types; it never carries an entity or aggregate, and the domain model does not shape itself after a contract (Evans: published language; Fowler: each context has its own model).
rules.fix: Declare a contract type with only the fields consumers need and map the entity to it in the application layer (or the published module); do not return or re-export the entity.
rules.applies: published places (public_api globs, contracts/, a context index.ts, inbound ports)

rules.title: a port signature carries an infrastructure type or mechanism
rules.rule: A port states what the application needs in its own terms; vendor types, adapter types and locking or transaction mechanisms stay inside the adapter (Cockburn, Ports and Adapters).
rules.fix: Express the need as an application-level operation (e.g. `reserve(roomId, dates)`) and keep the lock, transaction or vendor type inside the adapter that implements the port.
rules.applies: ports (application/ports, or domain interfaces implemented by an adapter)

rules.title: an application class depends on a concrete adapter class instead of a port
rules.rule: The application depends on ports; only the composition root knows the adapter classes (Cockburn; dependency inversion).
rules.fix: Type the dependency with the port interface the adapter implements (add one if missing) and construct the adapter in the composition root.
rules.applies: hexagonal and DDD styles (Layered services may depend on concrete persistence)

rules.title: a remote or vendor call runs inside a transaction or lock scope
rules.rule: A transaction or lock covers local state only; remote calls (payment, HTTP, vendor SDK) run before or after it, so a slow or failing remote never holds the lock (Nygard, Release It!: integration points).
rules.fix: Call the remote service outside the scoped callback (before it, or after commit through an event/outbox), and pass only its result into the transaction.

rules.title: a command of one bounded context persists an aggregate owned by another context in the same flow
rules.rule: A context changes only its own aggregates; another context's aggregate changes when that context reacts to a published event, not inside this command (Vernon; Evans, Bounded Context).
rules.fix: Record a domain event in this context (saved with this aggregate) and let the owning context subscribe to it through its published interface; do not call its write operation from this command.
rules.applies: contexts and aggregates declared in the spec's DDD block (or src/<context>/ folders)
